title: Red Hat Security Advisory: kernel security update
description: A security vulnerability in the Linux kernel's IPv4 implementation was identified and fixed by Red Hat. The issue involves improper validation of the checksum_start parameter before completing the checksum calculation. This vulnerability is tracked as CVE-2026-99999 and affects Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.4 versions. Red Hat has released a security update to address this issue and recommends applying the update and rebooting the system to ensure the fix takes effect.
aiSummary: The Linux kernel packages for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.4 contain a vulnerability in the IPv4 checksum validation process (CVE-2026-99999). Specifically, the kernel did not properly validate the checksum_start parameter before completing the checksum, which could lead to security issues. Red Hat has issued a security advisory (RHSA-2026:86089) and released updated kernel packages to fix this vulnerability. The update requires a system reboot to activate the patch. The advisory emphasizes the critical role of the kernel and recommends prompt application of the update to improve overall security posture.
aiImpact: The vulnerability affects the kernel's IPv4 checksum validation, which is fundamental to network packet processing. While the exact impact details are not fully described, Red Hat rates the security impact as Important (high severity). Exploitation could potentially affect system stability or security due to improper checksum validation. There are no known exploits in the wild at the time of the advisory.
